concepts.name: What an average represents
concepts.description: The value every member would have if the total were shared out equally.

concepts.name: Working with totals
concepts.description: Most average problems are solved by converting averages back into totals.

concepts.name: Combining groups
concepts.description: Merging two groups of different sizes — a weighted average in disguise.

concepts.name: Replacement and inclusion
concepts.description: What happens to the average when a member joins, leaves or is swapped.

concepts.name: Averages of sequences
concepts.description: Evenly spaced numbers average to their middle value.

formulas.title: Average
formulas.prompt: What is the formula for the average of a set of values?
formulas.formula: Average = Sum of values ÷ Number of values

variables.meaning: the total of all the values

formulas.explanation: The average redistributes the total equally among all members.
formulas.commonMistake: Dividing by the wrong count — recount the values before dividing.
formulas.applicationPrompt: You have five test scores and want the average. Which formula applies?

formulas.title: Total from an average
formulas.prompt: You know the average and the count. How do you get the total?
formulas.explanation: This is the single most useful rearrangement in the topic. Convert every average in a question into a total, and the problem becomes arithmetic.
formulas.commonMistake: Trying to work with averages directly instead of converting to totals first.
formulas.applicationPrompt: The average of 5 numbers is 18. Which formula gives their sum?

formulas.title: Combined average of two groups
formulas.prompt: Two groups of different sizes are merged. What is the combined average?
formulas.explanation: Add the totals, then divide by the combined count. The bigger group pulls the result towards its own average.
formulas.commonMistake: Averaging the two averages (65 here), which ignores the different group sizes.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Two classes of different sizes have different averages. Which formula gives the overall average?

formulas.title: Replacing a member
formulas.prompt: One member of a group is replaced and the average changes. How much did the total change?
formulas.formula: Change in total = n × change in average

variables.meaning: number of members (unchanged by a swap)

formulas.explanation: Because the count stays the same, the whole change in average comes from the difference between the person leaving and the person arriving.
formulas.example:
8 people, average rises 2.5 kg when a 65 kg person is replaced
Total rose by 8 × 2.5 = 20 kg
New person = 65 + 20 = 85 kg
formulas.commonMistake: Adding only the change in average (2.5) to the departing value.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A 65 kg member of an 8-person group is replaced and the average rises 2.5 kg. Which relationship finds the new member's weight?

formulas.title: Average of evenly spaced numbers
formulas.prompt: What is the average of a list of consecutive or evenly spaced numbers?
formulas.explanation: Evenly spaced values are symmetric about their middle, so the middle value is the average. No addition needed.
formulas.commonMistake: Using this on numbers that are not evenly spaced.
formulas.applicationPrompt: You need the average of five consecutive even numbers. What is the quickest route?

formulas.title: Shifting every value
formulas.prompt: Every value in a set increases by k. What happens to the average?
formulas.explanation: Adding the same amount to every member adds it to the average too. Multiplying every value by k multiplies the average by k.
formulas.example:
Average of a set is 40
Add 5 to every value → new average 45
formulas.commonMistake: Dividing the shift by the number of values — the shift carries over directly.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Every score in a class is raised by 5 marks. What happens to the class average?

formulas.title: Average by deviations
formulas.prompt: How do you average several close numbers without adding them all up?
formulas.formula: Average = Assumed value + (sum of deviations ÷ n)
formulas.explanation: Guess a convenient middle value; only the small differences from it need adding.
formulas.example: 48, 52, 55, 45 with assumed value 50: deviations −2, +2, +5, −5 sum to 0, so the average is 50.
formulas.commonMistake: Dropping the signs of the deviations.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Find the average of 97, 102, 105, 99 and 107 mentally.

formulas.title: Value of the one who joins
formulas.prompt: One more member joins a group of n and the average rises by k. What is the newcomer's value?
formulas.explanation: The newcomer must bring the new average for themselves, plus k extra for each of the n existing members.
formulas.example: 10 people average 40; one joins and the average becomes 41: newcomer = 41 + 10 × 1 = 51.
formulas.commonMistake: Multiplying the rise by n + 1 and adding it to the old average.
formulas.applicationPrompt: The average weight of 8 people rises by 2 kg when a ninth joins; the old average was 60 kg.

formulas.title: Averages of the first n numbers
formulas.prompt: What is the average of the first n natural, even and odd numbers?
formulas.formula:
First n natural numbers: (n + 1) ÷ 2
First n even numbers: n + 1
First n odd numbers: n
formulas.explanation: Each list is evenly spaced, so its average is (first + last) ÷ 2.
formulas.example: First 20 odd numbers (1 to 39): average 20. First 20 even numbers (2 to 40): average 21.
formulas.commonMistake: Using n ÷ 2 for the natural numbers and losing the half.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Find the average of the first 50 even numbers.

formulas.title: Correcting a misread value
formulas.prompt: One value was copied wrongly when an average of n values was found. What is the correct average?
formulas.formula: Correct average = Old average + (Correct value − Wrong value) ÷ n
formulas.explanation: The total is off by exactly the error, and that error is shared among all n values.
formulas.example: 20 values average 50, but a 65 was read as 45: 50 + 20 ÷ 20 = 51.
formulas.commonMistake: Adding the whole error to the average without dividing by n.
formulas.applicationPrompt: The mean of 25 marks was 60, but one mark of 84 had been entered as 48.

levels.title: Averages as Shared Totals
levels.description: One idea unlocks the topic: every average is a total waiting to be recovered.

blocks.title: An average is a fair share
blocks.body: If five people have ₹90 between them, the average is ₹18 — the amount each would hold if the money were shared equally. The average does not say anyone actually has ₹18.

blocks.title: Both directions matter
blocks.body: Average = Sum ÷ n        Sum = Average × n
blocks.caption: The second form is the one that solves exam questions.

blocks.body: Rule of thumb: the moment a question mentions an average, convert it into a total. Totals can be added, subtracted and compared; averages cannot.

blocks.title: Why totals win
blocks.body:
Average of 10 numbers is 25 → total = 250
Remove the number 34 → total = 216, count = 9
New average = 216 ÷ 9 = 24

Trying to do that in 'average language' alone is guesswork.

blocks.title: Averages sit between the extremes
blocks.body: An average is always between the smallest and largest value. If your answer falls outside that range, it is wrong — a two-second check worth doing every time.

levels.title: Average Formulas
levels.description: Six relationships, including the two shortcuts worth memorising.

levels.title: Identify the Pattern
levels.description: Decide whether a question is a total, a combination or a replacement.

levels.title: Direct Average Questions
levels.description: Finding averages and totals in a single step.

levels.title: Overlapping Groups
levels.description: The classic hard patterns: shared members, innings averages and hidden totals.

questions.question: What is the average of 12, 18, 24 and 30?
questions.explanation: Sum = 84 and there are 4 values, so the average is 84 ÷ 4 = 21.
questions.method: Sum ÷ count — or note the values are evenly spaced and take (12 + 30) ÷ 2.

hints.text: Add all four values first.
These numbers are evenly spaced, so (first + last) ÷ 2 also works.

questions.question: What is the average of the first 10 natural numbers?
questions.explanation: 1 to 10 sums to 55, and 55 ÷ 10 = 5.5. Or use (1 + 10) ÷ 2 = 5.5 since the numbers are evenly spaced.

hints.text: Consecutive numbers are evenly spaced.

commonMistakes: Answering 55, the sum rather than the average.

questions.question: The average of 5 numbers is 18. What is their sum?
questions.method: Convert the average into a total.

hints.text: Reverse the averaging: multiply instead of divide.

questions.question: The average of 4 numbers is 25. If one of the numbers is 40, what is the average of the other three?
questions.explanation: Total = 100. Removing 40 leaves 60 across three numbers, so their average is 20.

hints.text: Start by finding the total of all four numbers.
Subtract 40, then divide by 3.

commonMistakes: Subtracting 40 from the average rather than from the total.

questions.question: The average of 8 numbers is 21. A ninth number, 30, is added. Which expression gives the new average?
questions.explanation: Rebuild the total (8 × 21 = 168), add the new value, then divide by the new count of 9. The answer is 198 ÷ 9 = 22.
questions.method: Total, add, divide by the new count.

hints.text: You cannot average an average with a single value.
Rebuild the total first, then divide by 9.

questions.question: The average weight of 8 people rises by 1.5 kg when one member is replaced. What does that tell you?

options.text: The group's total weight rose by 8 × 1.5 = 12 kg
The new member weighs 1.5 kg more than the old one
The total weight rose by 1.5 kg

questions.explanation: The count is unchanged, so a 1.5 kg rise in the average means the total rose by 8 × 1.5 = 12 kg — and that entire gain is the difference between the two individuals.
solutionSteps: Replacement keeps the number of people at 8.
Change in total = number × change in average = 8 × 1.5 = 12 kg.
So the new member is 12 kg heavier than the one who left.
questions.method: Change in total = n × change in average.

hints.text: Every one of the 8 'slots' went up by 1.5 kg on paper.
Multiply the change in average by the group size.

commonMistakes: Assuming the difference between the two people is just 1.5 kg.

questions.question: If every number in a set is increased by 5, the average also increases by 5.
questions.explanation: With n values, the total rises by 5n, so the average rises by 5n ÷ n = 5.
solutionSteps: Each of the n values gains 5, so the total gains 5n.
questions.method: Track the change in total, then divide by n.

hints.text: How much does the TOTAL change by?
Try it with 10, 20, 30 — average 20 becomes 25.

commonMistakes: Assuming the shift must be divided by the number of values.

questions.question: The average of 10 numbers is 25. If the number 34 is removed, what is the average of the remaining numbers?
questions.explanation: Total = 250. After removing 34, the total is 216 across 9 numbers, giving 24.
questions.method: Total, subtract, re-divide by the new count.

hints.text: Convert the average into a total first.
Remember the count drops to 9.

commonMistakes: Dividing by 10 after removing a number.

questions.question: The average weight of 8 people increases by 2.5 kg when a new person replaces one weighing 65 kg. What is the new person's weight?
questions.explanation: The total rises by 8 × 2.5 = 20 kg, so the new person weighs 65 + 20 = 85 kg.
solutionSteps: That entire increase is the difference between the two people.
questions.method: Change in total = n × change in average.

hints.text: The group size does not change, so only one weight differs.
Total change = 8 × 2.5.
Add that change to 65.

commonMistakes: Answering 67.5 by adding only the change in average.

questions.question: A class of 20 students averages 60 marks and another class of 30 students averages 70 marks. What is the average of all 50 students?
questions.explanation: (20 × 60 + 30 × 70) ÷ 50 = (1200 + 2100) ÷ 50 = 66. The larger class pulls the average above the midpoint of 65.
questions.method: Weighted average: totals first, then divide by the combined count.

hints.text: The two classes are different sizes, so the plain midpoint is wrong.
Add the two totals, then divide by 50.

questions.question: The average of 5 consecutive even numbers is 22. What is the largest of them?
questions.explanation: For evenly spaced numbers the average is the middle value, so the numbers are 18, 20, 22, 24, 26 and the largest is 26.
solutionSteps: With an odd count of evenly spaced numbers, the average is the middle one: 22.
questions.method: Middle value = average for evenly spaced sets.

hints.text: Which of the five numbers must equal the average?
The middle number is 22 — build outwards in steps of 2.

questions.question: The average of 11 results is 50. The average of the first six is 49 and the average of the last six is 52. What is the sixth result?
questions.explanation: The sixth result is counted in both groups of six, so it equals (6 × 49) + (6 × 52) − (11 × 50) = 294 + 312 − 550 = 56.
solutionSteps: First six total = 294; last six total = 312; their sum is 606.
606 counts the sixth result twice, so the sixth result = 606 − 550 = 56.
questions.method: When two groups overlap, the overlap equals the sum of group totals minus the overall total.

hints.text: Six plus six is twelve, but there are only eleven results.
One result is included in both groups.
Overlap = (sum of the two group totals) − (overall total).

questions.question: A batsman scores 80 runs in his 17th innings, which raises his average by 3. What is his average after the 17th innings?
questions.explanation: Let the new average be x. Then 17x = 16(x − 3) + 80, giving x = 32.
solutionSteps: Let the average after 17 innings be x, so the average after 16 was x − 3.
Check: after 16 innings the average was 29 (total 464); 464 + 80 = 544 = 17 × 32 ✓
questions.method: Write the same total two ways and equate.

hints.text: Name the new average x and write the old one in terms of it.
Express the total after 17 innings in two different ways.

commonMistakes: Solving for the old average and reporting that instead.

questions.question: The average of 6 numbers is 30. The average of the first four is 25 and the average of the last three is 35. What is the fourth number?
questions.explanation: Total = 180. First four total 100 and last three total 105, summing to 205. The fourth number is counted twice, so it is 205 − 180 = 25.
solutionSteps: First four total = 4 × 25 = 100; last three total = 3 × 35 = 105.
questions.method: Overlap = sum of group totals − overall total.

hints.text: Four plus three is seven, but there are only six numbers.
Which position belongs to both groups?
Overlap = 205 − 180.

commonMistakes: Assuming the fourth number equals the overall average.
